meta.description: The 12 real examples from MoJ's '2026-09-29_Hackathon Evidence Examples.docx', in the same schema as synthetic_cases.json. Overall labels are MoJ's; element-level labels for rejections are inferred by comparing each rejected letter with its accepted pair. Keep these as a held-out test set.

I understand that Ms Jane Doe wishes to access legal aid for a family dispute as a victim of domestic violence. For this reason, I have been asked to provide a letter in accordance with regulation 33 and schedule 1 of the Civil Legal Aid (Procedure) Regulations 2012 (as amended).

I can confirm that our organisation is situated in England and Wales and has been operating for an uninterrupted period of six months or more.

I can confirm that we have provided Ms Doe support in relation to their needs as a victim, or person at risk of domestic violence.

In my reasonable professional judgement Ms Doe was a victim, or a person at risk of domestic violence.

The matters I have relied upon to support that judgement are: disclosures surrounding emotional, physical and psychological abuse with coercive and controlling behaviour.

We have provided Ms Doe with the following support: risk assessment, safety planning and referrals for emotional support.

Ms Doe needed this support because she is a victim, or a person at risk of domestic abuse from her ex-partner.

I understand that Joe Bloggs wishes to access legal aid for a family dispute as a victim of domestic violence. For this reason, I have been asked to provide a letter in accordance with regulation 33 and schedule 1 of the Civil Legal Aid (Procedure) Regulations 2012 (as amended).

I can confirm that our organisation is situated in England and Wales and has been operating for an uninterrupted period of six months or more.

I can confirm that we have provided Joe Bloggs with support in relation to their needs as a victim, or a person at risk, of domestic violence.

In my reasonable professional judgement, Joe Bloggs is, or is at risk of being, a victim of domestic violence.

The matters I have relied upon to support that judgement are; Refuge space being granted for Joe and their son following a referral taken and DASH score being 12 and current statements being given to the police in regards to the abuse that has happened, the hope of a court date and possible conviction for the perpetrator.

We have provided Joe Bloggs the following support: Support for health concerns and registering with GP, support to report the crimes and attend the station to give a statement, Domestic Violence education.

Joe Bloggs needed this support because: They fled their home due to fear for their life. Joe is willing to accept support in other areas such as emotional wellbeing.

documents.text:
I understand Jane Smith wishes to access legal aid for a family dispute as a victim of domestic violence. For this reason, I have been asked to provide a letter in accordance with regulation 33 and schedule 1 of the Civil Legal Aid (Procedure) Regulations 2012 (as amended).

I can confirm that our organisation is situated in England and Wales and has been operating for an uninterrupted period of six months or more.

I can confirm that we have provided Jane Smith with support in relation to their needs as a victim, or person at risk, of domestic violence.

In my reasonable professional judgement Jane Smith is, or is at risk of being, a vicim of domestic violence.

The matters I have relied upon to support that judgement are:

- Jane has told me that her ex would tell her about all the local mums he had slept with. When she did not respond he would tell her he hoped she dies in her sleep.

- Jane has told me her ex was extremely controlling, his anger and controlling behaviour would get out of control and he would be shouting, calling her names and would belittle her.

- Jane has told me that her ex did not like her working, he used to say how he did not liker her work colleagues or friends. He would say they were toxic and negative. She was not allowed to discussion anything to do with work in the home and she was prevented from discussing her home life in work.

- She has told me that he made it clear he did not like her friends and would say they were toxic. He would check her phone daily and read her messages and question her about them. Jane stopped interacting with her friends and family as it was easier to not receive any to avoid being questioned and him getting angry and abusive. She felt isolated as a result.

- Jane said she always felt on edge. She told me she lost herself trying to please him so he would not get angry or abusive with her in the home.

- Jane has told me how her ex would demand sec and give her the silent treatment if she said no. Jane said that in the end he would ignore that she had said not to him. He would often want sex when she was asleep and ignore that she was asleep.

- Jane has told me that he attended a funeral and afterwards drunk and smashed the house up which was witnessed by their daughter.

We have provided Jane Smith the following support: Helpline support and advice, including risk assessment, followed by ongoing attendance and engagement in a programme specialising in group support for recovery of adults who have experienced domestic abuse.

Jane Smith needed this support because they were identified as a victim of domestic abuse.

I understand that Jane Doe wishes to access legal aid for a family dispute as a victim of domestic violence. For this reason I have been asked to provide a letter in accordance with regulation 33 of the Civil Legal Aid (Procedure) Regulations 2012.

The applicant has confirmed that the condition that she presented to me with today was caused by domestic abuse.

I can confirm that I have examined Jane Doe and in my reasonable professional judgement, the condition that the applicant has is consistent with domestic abuse.

I understand that this evidence is only required for a decision on whether or not to grant legal aid – it is not designed to provide evidence of domestic abuse for use in court.

documents.text:
To whom it may concern

Name of perpetrator: John Doe

Name of applicant: Jane Doe

I understand that Jane Doe wishes to access legal aid for a family dispute as a victim of domestic abuse. For this reason, I have been asked to provide a letter in accordance with regulation 33 and schedule 1 of the Civil Legal Aid (Procedure) Regulations 2012 (as amended).

Accordingly, I can confirm that Jane Doe, a person with whom John Doe is or was in a family relationship with, was assessed as being, or at risk of being, a victim of domestic abuse by John Doe.

More information and guidance about the evidential requirements for legal aid can be found at: https://www.gov.uk/legal-aid/domestic-abuse

Yours sincerely,

John Smith

Bath and Northeast Somerset Council
